title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

target.split: Test = 50% of documents not used as normal training data (normal + anomalous); token-level scoring over test documents

text: Cloning into 'repo'...

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation

   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38|

    1| from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    2| import numpy as np
    3| 
    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

import json

d = np.load('repo/data/grammar.npy', allow_pickle=True).item()

print('sent[0]:', sents[0])
print('tok[0]:', toks[0])
print('lab[0]:', labs[0])

doc_lab = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labs]
print('n anomalous docs:', sum(doc_lab), 'n normal:', len(doc_lab) - sum(doc_lab))
n_tok = sum(len(t) for t in toks)
n_pos = sum(int(x) for l in labs for x in l)
print('total tokens:', n_tok, 'positive tokens:', n_pos, 'rate:', n_pos / n_tok)

# label value set
vals = sorted({x for l in labs for x in l})
print('label values:', vals)

# do anomalous docs come last? print doc_label pattern
print('doc labels first 20:', doc_lab[:20])
print('doc labels around anomaly boundary:')
idx_anom = [i for i, y in enumerate(doc_lab) if y == 1]
print('first anomalous idx:', idx_anom[:5], 'last:', idx_anom[-3:])
print('contiguous block?', idx_anom == list(range(idx_anom[0], idx_anom[0] + len(idx_anom))))

# JSON schema
j = json.load(open('repo/data/grammar_correction_labeled.json', encoding='utf-8'))
print('json type:', type(j), 'len:', len(j))
print('json[0] keys:', list(j[0].keys()))
print('json[0] data keys:', list(j[0]['data'].keys()))
print('json[0] sentence:', str(j[0]['data'])[:300])
print('json[0] annotation result[:2]:', json.dumps(j[0]['annotations'][0]['result'][:2])[:500])

# check tokens of anomalous docs
for i in idx_anom[:3]:
    marked = [t for t, l in zip(toks[i], labs[i]) if l == 1]
    print(f'anom doc {i}: marked tokens: {marked}')
    print('   full:', ' '.join(toks[i])[:200])

"""Load the released Grammar benchmark (authors' data/grammar.npy) and apply the
authors' train/test split.

Source of the split logic: the upstream repository ships
__pycache__/eval.cpython-310.pyc (bytecode of the missing eval.py referenced by
Demo.ipynb).  Disassembling that bytecode with xdis recovers `split_anomaly_data`
verbatim, including its defaults train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42:

    def split_anomaly_data(X, y, z, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
        y = np.array(y)
        n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio)
        normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
        np.random.seed(random_state)
        train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, size=n_train, replace=False)
        test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(X)), train_indices)
        X_train = [X[i] for i in train_indices]
        y_train = y[train_indices]
        X_test  = [X[i] for i in test_indices]
        y_test  = y[test_indices]
        z_train = [z[i] for i in train_indices]
        z_test  = [z[i] for i in test_indices]
        return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

Note `n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio)` is 50% of ALL documents (150 for
Grammar), drawn from the normal indices only, so the training set never contains
an anomalous token (paper Sec 6.1: "We use 50% normal documents as training
data, the rest of data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly").
"""
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np

REPO_DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo" / "data"

# Paper Sec 4 (R10): 300 documents, 270 normal + 30 anomalous (10% rate).
EXPECTED_N_DOCS = 300
EXPECTED_N_ANOM = 30


def load_grammar(npz_path=None):
    """Return (tokens, labels, doc_labels): word tokens, per-token 0/1 labels and
    per-document 0/1 labels for the 300-document Grammar benchmark."""
    path = Path(npz_path) if npz_path is not None else REPO_DATA / "grammar.npy"
    data = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens = [[str(t) for t in doc] for doc in data["tokens"]]
    labels = [[int(x) for x in doc] for doc in data["labels"]]
    assert len(tokens) == len(labels) == EXPECTED_N_DOCS, (
        f"expected {EXPECTED_N_DOCS} documents, got {len(tokens)}")

    doc_labels = [int(any(l)) for l in labels]
    n_anom = sum(doc_labels)
    assert n_anom == EXPECTED_N_ANOM, (
        f"expected {EXPECTED_N_ANOM} anomalous documents, got {n_anom} (R10)")
    assert len(tokens) - n_anom == EXPECTED_N_DOCS - EXPECTED_N_ANOM

    # R11: document is anomalous iff it contains at least one anomalous token.
    for t, l, d in zip(tokens, labels, doc_labels):
        assert len(t) == len(l), "token/label length mismatch"
        assert d == int(any(l)), "document label inconsistent with token labels"

    return tokens, labels, doc_labels


def split_anomaly_data(X, y, z, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
    """Verbatim re-implementation of the authors' eval.split_anomaly_data
    (recovered from __pycache__/eval.cpython-310.pyc, see module docstring)."""
    y = np.array(y)
    n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio)
    normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
    np.random.seed(random_state)
    train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, size=n_train, replace=False)
    test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(X)), train_indices)
    X_train = [X[i] for i in train_indices]
    y_train = y[train_indices]
    X_test = [X[i] for i in test_indices]
    y_test = y[test_indices]
    z_train = [z[i] for i in train_indices]
    z_test = [z[i] for i in test_indices]
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test


def describe_split(tokens, labels, doc_labels, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
    """Apply the authors' split at document level and report the sizes/counts."""
    X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = split_anomaly_data(
        tokens, doc_labels, labels, train_ratio=train_ratio, random_state=random_state)
    assert int(np.sum(y_train)) == 0, "training documents must all be normal (R3/R6)"
    assert int(np.sum(y_test)) == EXPECTED_N_ANOM, "all anomalous docs must be in test"
    info = {
        "n_docs": len(tokens),
        "n_train_docs": len(X_train),
        "n_test_docs": len(X_test),
        "n_test_normal_docs": int(len(X_test) - np.sum(y_test)),
        "n_test_anom_docs": int(np.sum(y_test)),
        "n_train_tokens": sum(len(t) for t in X_train),
        "n_test_tokens": sum(len(t) for t in X_test),
        "n_test_positive_tokens": int(sum(sum(l) for l in z_test)),
        "n_total_tokens": sum(len(t) for t in tokens),
        "n_total_positive_tokens": int(sum(sum(l) for l in labels)),
        "train_ratio": train_ratio,
        "random_state": random_state,
    }
    return info, (X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test)

"""BERT-base front-end: contextual subword embeddings -> word-level embeddings by
element-wise max pooling over the subwords of each word (paper Eq. (1), R2/R9).

This reproduces the per-sentence behaviour of the authors' align.py
extract_word_embeddings (Demo.ipynb cell 2/3), batched for speed:
  * tokenizer(words, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True)
  * last_hidden_state of the BERT model
  * [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] are dropped (word_ids() is None)
  * each word's subword vectors are aggregated with np.max(stack, axis=0)
Every document must yield exactly one word unit per gold token, so the output
stays aligned with the word-level token annotations.
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 32
DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH = 512  # authors' align.py uses the tokenizer default


def _hf_cache_dir():
    """Keep the (large, reusable) HF model cache under REPRO_DATA_CACHE."""
    root = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    hf_home = os.environ.get("HF_HOME")
    if hf_home:
        return Path(hf_home)
    if root:
        return Path(root) / "hf"
    return Path.home() / ".cache" / "huggingface"


def load_model(model_name):
    os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", str(_hf_cache_dir()))
    os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS_WARNING", "1")
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model.eval()
    return tokenizer, model


def extract_word_embeddings(tokenizer, model, docs_tokens, batch_size=DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE,
                            max_length=DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH, device=None, desc=""):
    """Return one (n_words, hidden) float32 matrix per document.

    Word units are 1:1 with the input token lists (asserted), so downstream
    token labels align positionally (R9).
    """
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    hidden = model.config.hidden_size

    all_emb = []
    n_batches = (len(docs_tokens) + batch_size - 1) // batch_size
    with torch.no_grad():
        for b in range(n_batches):
            chunk = docs_tokens[b * batch_size:(b + 1) * batch_size]
            enc = tokenizer(
                chunk,
                is_split_into_words=True,
                return_tensors="pt",
                truncation=True,
                max_length=max_length,
                padding=True,
            )
            enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
            out = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
            last_hidden = out.last_hidden_state  # (B, T, H)

            for j in range(len(chunk)):
                word_ids = enc_word_ids(tokenizer, chunk, j, b, batch_size, enc,
                                        docs_tokens, b * batch_size + j)
                vecs = last_hidden[j]
                doc_emb, current = [], []

                def flush():
                    if current:
                        # Eq. (1): element-wise max over the word's subwords.
                        doc_emb.append(np.max(np.stack(current), axis=0))

                prev = None
                del doc_emb[:]
                del current[:]
                for pos, w in enumerate(word_ids):
                    if w is None:
                        continue  # [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]
                    if prev is not None and w != prev:
                        flush()
                        del current[:]
                    current.append(vecs[pos].float().cpu().numpy())
                    prev = w
                flush()

                emb = np.asarray(doc_emb, dtype=np.float32)
                assert emb.shape == (len(chunk[j]), hidden), (
                    f"alignment failed: doc {b * batch_size + j} produced "
                    f"{emb.shape[0]} word units for {len(chunk[j])} gold tokens")
                all_emb.append(emb)
    return all_emb


def enc_word_ids(tokenizer, chunk, j, b, batch_size, enc, docs_tokens, global_idx):
    """word_ids() for row j of the batch; falls back to a single-doc re-tokenization."""
    try:
        return enc["input_ids"].new_tensor([]) and tokenizer_enc_word_ids(enc, j)
    except Exception:
        pass
    single = tokenizer(chunk[j], is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True,
                       max_length=DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH)
    return single.word_ids(batch_index=0)


def tokenizer_enc_word_ids(enc, j):
    """BatchEncoding.word_ids for row j (works across transformers versions)."""
    try:
        wi = enc.word_ids(batch_index=j)
    except TypeError:
        wi = enc.word_ids(j)
    if wi is None:
        raise RuntimeError("word_ids unavailable")
    return list(wi)

import numpy as np
import torch

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model.eval()

    """word_ids() for row j of a batch, robust across transformers versions."""

                           max_length=DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH)

                            batch_size=DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE,

            chunk = docs_tokens[lo:lo + batch_size]
            enc = tokenizer(
                chunk,
                is_split_into_words=True,
                return_tensors="pt",
                truncation=True,
                max_length=max_length,
                padding=True,
            )
            out = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"],
                        attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
            last_hidden = out.last_hidden_state  # (B, T, H)

            for j, doc_tokens in enumerate(chunk):
                word_ids = batch_word_ids(enc, j, tokenizer, doc_tokens)
                vecs = last_hidden[j]
                doc_emb = []
                current = []
                prev = None

                def flush():
                    if current:
                        # Eq. (1): element-wise max over the word's subword vectors.
                        doc_emb.append(np.max(np.stack(current), axis=0))

                for pos, w in enumerate(word_ids):
                    if w is None:

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified TokenCore.py.

The authors' file (repo/TokenCore.py) defines

    class TokenCore:
        def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max')
        def fit(X)                      -> NearestNeighbors(...).fit(X)
        def decision_function(X)        -> distance to the nearest bank entry

which is exactly the memory bank + nearest-neighbour scoring of paper Eq. (2)
(R3/R4).  Demo.ipynb imports it as `TextCore` (`from TextCore import TextCore`);
the class name in the released file is TokenCore, so the adapter resolves
whichever name the file actually exposes and never modifies the authors' code.
"""
import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo"


def load_authors_detector(repo_path=None, n_neighbors=1, aggregation="max"):
    path = (Path(repo_path) if repo_path else REPO / "TokenCore.py").resolve()
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("authors_tokencore", path)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    cls = None
    for name in ("TokenCore", "TextCore"):
        if hasattr(mod, name):
            cls = getattr(mod, name)
            break
    if cls is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"no TokenCore/TextCore class found in {path}")
    return cls(n_neighbors=n_neighbors, aggregation=aggregation)


def fit_memory_bank(X_train, n_neighbors=1, aggregation="max"):
    """Fit the authors' detector on the full normal-token memory bank (R3, A2)."""
    model = load_authors_detector(n_neighbors=n_neighbors, aggregation=aggregation)
    model.fit(X_train)
    return model


def score_tokens(model, X_test):
    """One nearest-neighbour (L2) distance per test token (R4, A1); higher = more anomalous."""
    scores = model.decision_function(X_test)

"""Metric layer (R7).

Conventions (recovered from the authors' bytecode eval.evaluate_model and
Demo.ipynb, plus paper Eq. (3)):
  * token-level AUROC  = sklearn roc_auc_score over ALL test tokens pooled
    (Demo.ipynb cell 4: roc_auc_score(z_test, score)).
  * token-level AUPRC  = auc(recall, precision) from sklearn precision_recall_curve
    (authors' eval.py evaluate_model); average_precision_score is also reported
    as a cross-check since the two differ slightly.
  * document score     = mean of the document's token scores (paper Eq. (3));
    the authors' eval.py uses np.max, so the max variant is reported too.
"""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import (average_precision_score, auc, precision_recall_curve,
                             roc_auc_score)


def pr_auc(recall_precision_style=True):
    raise NotImplementedError


def token_auroc(y_true, scores):
    return float(roc_auc_score(np.asarray(y_true), np.asarray(scores)))


def token_auprc(y_true, scores):
    """Authors' convention: auc(recall, precision) via precision_recall_curve."""
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(np.asarray(y_true), np.asarray(scores))
    return float(auc(recall, precision))


def token_average_precision(y_true, scores):
    return float(average_precision_score(np.asarray(y_true), np.asarray(scores)))


def aggregate_document_scores(scores, doc_lengths, how="mean"):
    """Paper Eq. (3): aggregate token scores within a document.

    how='mean' -> arithmetic mean (paper Eq. (3), R5)
    how='max'  -> np.max (authors' eval.py evaluate_model)
    """
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    out = []
    start = 0
    for length in doc_lengths:
        end = start + length
        seg = scores[start:end]
        if how == "mean":
            out.append(float(np.mean(seg)))
        elif how == "max":
            out.append(float(np.max(seg)))
        else:
            raise ValueError(how)
        start = end
    assert start == len(scores), "doc_lengths must cover every token score"
    return np.asarray(out, dtype=np.float64)


def all_metrics(y_tok, scores, doc_lengths, doc_labels):
    y_tok = np.asarray(y_tok)
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    doc_labels = np.asarray(doc_labels)
    out = {}
    out["token_auroc"] = token_auroc(y_tok, scores)
    out["token_auprc"] = token_auprc(y_tok, scores)
    out["token_average_precision"] = token_average_precision(y_tok, scores)
    for how in ("mean", "max"):
        dscores = aggregate_document_scores(scores, doc_lengths, how=how)
        out[f"doc_auroc_{how}"] = token_auroc(doc_labels, dscores)
        out[f"doc_auprc_{how}"] = token_auprc(doc_labels, dscores)
    return out


def metric_parity_check(n_pos=10, n_neg=200, seed=0):
    """Validate this module against sklearn on synthetic labels (plan check)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    y = np.zeros(n_pos + n_neg, dtype=int)
    y[:n_pos] = 1
    s = y * 1.0 + rng.normal(0, 1, size=y.shape)
    assert abs(token_auroc(y, s) - roc_auc_score(y, s)) < 1e-12
    assert abs(token_average_precision(y, s) - average_precision_score(y, s)) < 1e-12
    # an intentionally reversed score must fall below 0.5
    assert token_auroc(y, -s) < 0.5
    return True


def random_control(y_tok, doc_lengths, doc_labels, seed=0):
    """Random scores should give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~ the positive rate."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    scores = rng.random(len(y_tok))
    y_tok = np.asarray(y_tok)
    pos_rate = float(np.mean(y_tok))
    return {
        "random_token_auroc": token_auroc(y_tok, scores),
        "random_token_auprc": token_auprc(y_tok, scores),
        "random_token_average_precision": token_average_precision(y_tok, scores),
        "positive_token_rate": pos_rate,
    }

"""Reproduce the TokenCore token-level results on the Grammar benchmark.

Target claim C1/C2 (paper Table 1, Token section, Grammar column):
TokenCore token-level AUROC/AUPRC with
  * BERT-base-uncased contextual embeddings, element-wise max pooling over
    subwords -> word units (paper Eq. (1), R2/R9)
  * memory bank of ALL token embeddings of the normal training documents (R3)
  * nearest-neighbour L2 distance as the token anomaly score (paper Eq. (2), R4)
  * 50% of the documents (drawn from the normal ones) as training data, the
    remaining normal + all anomalous documents as the test set (R6)
Document-level scores are the mean of the token scores (paper Eq. (3), R5);
the authors' eval.py np.max variant is reported as a diagnostic.

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                 # full Grammar run, primary seed + spread
  python reproduce.py --smoke         # 10-document end-to-end smoke test
  python reproduce.py --seed 42 --spread-seeds 0,1,2
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_anomaly_data          # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, extract_word_embeddings, load_model  # noqa: E402
from detector import fit_memory_bank, score_tokens                  # noqa: E402

SPREAD_SEEDS = [0, 1, 2]
SMOKE_N_NORMAL = 8
SMOKE_N_ANOM = 2

def set_torch_threads():
    import torch
    n = max(1, min(8, os.cpu_count() or 1))

def claim_target_from_plan():
    """The paper's target value lives in state/plan.json (config.target_value).
    It is read from there - never hardcoded - and used only for the pass/fail band."""
    try:
        plan = json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "plan.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        raw = plan["config"]["target_value"]
        m = re.search(r"([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", str(raw))
        return float(m.group(1)) if m else None, str(raw)
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        log(f"could not read claim target from state/plan.json: {exc}")
        return None, None


def select_docs(tokens, labels, doc_labels, n_normal, n_anom):
    """Deterministic smoke subset: first n_normal normal + first n_anom anomalous."""
    normal_idx = [i for i, d in enumerate(doc_labels) if d == 0][:n_normal]
    anom_idx = [i for i, d in enumerate(doc_labels) if d == 1][:n_anom]
    keep = sorted(normal_idx + anom_idx)

def data_md5(path):
    return hashlib.md5(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]


def emb_cache_path(backbone, dataset, key):
    root = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if not root:
        return None
    d = Path(root) / "tokencore_embeddings"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d / f"{dataset}_{backbone.replace('/', '_')}_{key}.npz"


def load_or_compute_embeddings(tokens, backbone, batch_size, cache_key, use_cache=True):
    """Embeddings do not depend on the split: compute once for all documents."""
    path = emb_cache_path(backbone, "grammar", cache_key) if use_cache else None

                   expect_full=True):
    """Apply the authors' split at document level and report the sizes/counts.

    expect_full=True keeps the strict paper checks (300 docs / 30 anomalous, R10);
    expect_full=False (smoke subsets) only checks what must hold for ANY subset:
    the training half is all-normal and every anomalous input document lands in
    the test set.
    """
    X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = split_anomaly_data(
        tokens, doc_labels, labels, train_ratio=train_ratio, random_state=random_state)
    assert int(np.sum(y_train)) == 0, "training documents must all be normal (R3/R6)"
    n_anom_in_input = int(np.sum(doc_labels))
    assert int(np.sum(y_test)) == n_anom_in_input, \
        "every anomalous document in the input must land in the test set"
    if expect_full:
        assert len(tokens) == EXPECTED_N_DOCS, \

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
d = np.load('repo/data/grammar.npy', allow_pickle=True).item()
docs = [list(x) for x in d['tokens']]

# doc 0 diagnostics under different tokenizer options
for label, kw in [('plain', {}), ('padding', dict(padding=True)),
                  ('truncation', dict(truncation=True)),
                  ('both', dict(padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=512))]:
    enc = tok([docs[0]], is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors='pt', **kw)
    print(label, 'tokens:', enc.tokens(0))
    print(label, 'word_ids:', enc.word_ids(0))

# whole-dataset multi-subword census (batch, no truncation)
multi = 0
examples = []
bad_align = 0
for i in range(0, len(docs), 64):
    chunk = docs[i:i + 64]
    enc = tok(chunk, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors='pt', padding=True)
    for j, doc in enumerate(chunk):
        wi = enc.word_ids(batch_index=j)
        toks = enc.tokens(batch_index=j)
        # 1:1 mapping check: every gold word index 0..len-1 must appear, nothing else
        ids = {w for w in wi if w is not None}
        if ids != set(range(len(doc))):
            bad_align += 1
            if bad_align <= 3:
                print(f'MISALIGNED doc {i+j}: gold {len(doc)} words, word ids {sorted(ids)[:10]}..., toks {toks[:15]}')
        c = Counter(w for w in wi if w is not None)
        for w, n in c.items():
            if n > 1:
                multi += 1
                if len(examples) < 10:
                    subwords = [t for t, x in zip(toks, wi) if x == w]
                    examples.append((i + j, doc[w], subwords))
print('docs with word-id misalignment:', bad_align)
print('total multi-subword words in Grammar:', multi)
for e in examples:
    print('  example:', e)

def pooling_unit_check(tokenizer, model, all_tokens, embs, max_length=512):
    """Plan check: the word embedding really is the coordinate-wise max of the
    word's subword vectors (Eq. 1), and not e.g. the first subword or the mean.

    Censuses the FULL document set (not the smoke subset) at the tokenizer level,
    asserting for every document that the gold-token -> word-unit mapping is 1:1
    (R9/A4).  The first multi-subword word found anywhere is then verified
    against its stored embedding when that document was embedded, or against a
    fresh solo extraction otherwise.  If the dataset genuinely contains no
    multi-subword word, the first 20 word/token units are printed and the
    absence is reported instead of asserted.
    """
    import torch
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    multi = None
    B = 64
    for lo in range(0, len(all_tokens), B):
        chunk = all_tokens[lo:lo + B]
        enc = tokenizer(chunk, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                        padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=max_length)
        for j, doc in enumerate(chunk):
            wi = list(enc.word_ids(batch_index=j))
            ids = {w for w in wi if w is not None}
            if ids != set(range(len(doc))):
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"gold-token -> word-unit mapping is NOT 1:1 for document "
                    f"{lo + j}: {len(doc)} gold tokens vs word ids {sorted(ids)} "
                    f"(R9/A4)")
            if multi is None:
                groups = {}
                for pos, w in enumerate(wi):
                    if w is not None:
                        groups.setdefault(w, []).append(pos)
                for w, poss in groups.items():
                    if len(poss) > 1:
                        multi = (lo + j, w, poss)
                        break
    if multi is None:
        # No multi-subword unit exists anywhere: the 1:1 mapping (the thing that
        # actually matters for R9/A4) has been verified for every document above.
        n_printed = 0
        for d_i, doc in enumerate(all_tokens[:5]):
            enc = tokenizer([doc], is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True,
                            max_length=max_length)
            toks = enc.tokens(batch_index=0)
            wi = enc.word_ids(batch_index=0)
            for w in range(len(doc)):
                subs = [t for t, x in zip(toks, wi) if x == w]
                print(f"    doc {d_i} gold token {w} {doc[w]!r} -> subwords {subs}")
                n_printed += 1
                if n_printed >= 20:
                    break
            if n_printed >= 20:
                break
        print("[reproduce] no multi-subword word exists in this dataset; "
              "1:1 gold-token -> word-unit mapping verified for all documents")
        return 0, None, 1, False

    doc_i, w, poss = multi
    if doc_i < len(embs) and embs[doc_i].shape[0] == len(all_tokens[doc_i]):
        stored = np.asarray(embs[doc_i][w])
        source = "stored batched extraction"
    else:
        # the document is outside the embedded subset (smoke mode): extract solo
        solo = extract_word_embeddings(tokenizer, model, [all_tokens[doc_i]],
                                       batch_size=1, max_length=max_length)
        stored = solo[0][w]
        source = "fresh solo extraction"
    with torch.no_grad():
        enc = tokenizer([all_tokens[doc_i]], is_split_into_words=True,
                        return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=max_length)
        out = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"].to(device),
                    attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"].to(device))
    vecs = out.last_hidden_state[0]
    sub = [vecs[p].float().cpu().numpy() for p in poss]
    pooled = np.max(np.stack(sub), axis=0)
    assert np.allclose(pooled, stored, atol=1e-4), "max pooling mismatch"
    assert not np.allclose(np.asarray(sub[0]), stored, atol=1e-4), (
        "word vector equals the FIRST subword - pooling not applied")
    mean_pool = np.mean(np.stack(sub), axis=0)
    assert not np.allclose(mean_pool, stored, atol=1e-4), (
        "word vector equals the MEAN of subwords - pooling not applied")
    print(f"[reproduce] pooling verified on '{all_tokens[doc_i][w]}' "
          f"({len(sub)} subwords, doc {doc_i}, {source})")
    return doc_i, all_tokens[doc_i][w], len(sub), True

                f"{len(doc)} gold tokens vs word ids {sorted(ids)} (R9/A4)")
        groups = {}
        for pos, w in enumerate(wi):
            if w is not None:
                groups.setdefault(w, []).append(pos)
        for w, poss in groups.items():
            if len(poss) > 1:
                multi = (doc_i, w, poss)
                break
        if multi:
            break

    if multi is None:
        # No multi-subword unit exists anywhere: the 1:1 mapping (the thing that
        # actually matters for R9/A4) has been verified for every document above.
        n_printed = 0
        for d_i, doc in enumerate(tokens[:5]):
            enc = tokenizer([doc], is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True,
                            max_length=max_length)
            toks = enc.tokens(batch_index=0)
            wi = enc.word_ids(batch_index=0)
            for w in range(len(doc)):
                subs = [t for t, x in zip(toks, wi) if x == w]
                print(f"    doc {d_i} gold token {w} {doc[w]!r} -> subwords {subs}")
                n_printed += 1
                if n_printed >= 20:
                    break
            if n_printed >= 20:
                break
        print("[reproduce] no multi-subword word exists in this dataset; "
              "1:1 gold-token -> word-unit mapping verified for all documents")
        return 0, None, 1, False

    doc_i, w, poss = multi
    with torch.no_grad():
        enc = tokenizer([tokens[doc_i]], is_split_into_words=True,
                        return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=max_length)
        out = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"].to(device),
                    attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"].to(device))
    vecs = out.last_hidden_state[0]
    sub = [vecs[p].float().cpu().numpy() for p in poss]
    pooled = np.max(np.stack(sub), axis=0)
    stored = embs[doc_i][w]
    assert np.allclose(pooled, stored, atol=1e-4), "max pooling mismatch"
    assert not np.allclose(np.asarray(sub[0]), stored, atol=1e-4), (
        "word vector equals the FIRST subword - pooling not applied")
    mean_pool = np.mean(np.stack(sub), axis=0)
    assert not np.allclose(mean_pool, stored, atol=1e-4), (
        "word vector equals the MEAN of subwords - pooling not applied")
    return doc_i, tokens[doc_i][w], len(sub), True

"""Run the authors' demo path UNMODIFIED on the released grammar.npy, for both
backbones, to localise the C1 gap to extraction vs scoring.

Everything here is the authors' code, called exactly as demo.ipynb does:
  cell 0: data load + sentence_labels + eval.split_anomaly_data(DEFAULTS)
  cell 2/3: align.extract_word_embeddings(model=None, tokenizer=None, ...)
  cell 4: TextCore(); model.fit(X_train); score = model.decision_function(X_test);
          roc_auc_score(z_test, score)
Only the model_name (bert-base-cased as in the notebook vs bert-base-uncased as
in the paper text) is varied.  Document-level mean/max AUROC is computed from
the same scores for completeness.
"""
import contextlib
import io
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src"))
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", os.path.join(
    os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ""), "hf"))

from align import extract_word_embeddings            # authors', verbatim
from TokenCore import TokenCore as TextCore          # authors', verbatim
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, precision_recall_curve, auc


def pr_auc(y, s):
    p, r, _ = precision_recall_curve(y, s)
    return auc(r, p)


def doc_scores(scores, lengths, how="mean"):
    out, i = [], 0
    for n in lengths:
        seg = scores[i:i + n]
        out.append(float(np.mean(seg)) if how == "mean" else float(np.max(seg)))
        i += n
    return np.array(out)


data = np.load(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo/data/grammar.npy",
               allow_pickle=True).item()
tokens, labels = data["tokens"], data["labels"]
sentence_labels = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labels]          # demo cell 0
X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = None, None, None, None, None, None

# demo cell 0 calls eval.split_anomaly_data(tokens, sentence_labels, labels) with
# defaults; the recovered implementation lives in src/data_grammar.py
from data_grammar import split_anomaly_data
X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = split_anomaly_data(
    tokens, sentence_labels, labels)

for backbone in ("bert-base-uncased", "bert-base-cased"):
    print(f"\n=== authors' demo path, backbone={backbone} ===", flush=True)
    # cell 2: train extraction (model=None/tokenizer=None -> their loader)
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        train_data = extract_word_embeddings(model=None, tokenizer=None,
                                             all_tokens=X_train, all_labels=z_train,
                                             model_name=backbone,
                                             local_cache_dir=os.environ["HF_HOME"],
                                             device="cpu")
    Xtr = np.array([it["embedding"] for sent in train_data for it in sent])
    # cell 3: test extraction
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        test_data = extract_word_embeddings(model=None, tokenizer=None,
                                            all_tokens=X_test, all_labels=z_test,
                                            model_name=backbone,
                                            local_cache_dir=os.environ["HF_HOME"],
                                            device="cpu")
    Xte = np.array([it["embedding"] for sent in test_data for it in sent])
    zte = [it["label"] for sent in test_data for it in sent]
    lengths = [len(s) for s in test_data]

    # cell 4: scoring + pooled metric (authors', verbatim)
    model = TextCore()
    model.fit(Xtr)
    score = model.decision_function(Xte)
    token_roc = roc_auc_score(zte, score)

    doc_mean = roc_auc_score(y_test, doc_scores(score, lengths, "mean"))
    doc_max = roc_auc_score(y_test, doc_scores(score, lengths, "max"))
    print(f"token AUROC = {token_roc:.4f}  token AUPRC = {pr_auc(zte, score):.4f}  "
          f"doc AUROC mean = {doc_mean:.4f}  max = {doc_max:.4f}  "
          f"(n_bank={Xtr.shape[0]}, n_test_tok={Xte.shape[0]}, "
          f"pos={int(np.sum(zte))})", flush=True)

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The reproduction implements the TokenCore pipeline faithfully for the C1 target: BERT-base-uncased last-hidden-state embeddings, element-wise max pooling over subwords (asserted against first-subword and mean-pooling alternatives), a memory bank of all 1,327 normal-training token embeddings with an assertion that no anomalous token enters it, Euclidean nearest-neighbour token scoring, and pooled-token AUROC/AUPRC computed exactly as the authors' recovered eval.evaluate_model does. The split is the authors' own recovered split_anomaly_data (150 of 300 documents drawn from the 270 normal ones, seed 42), which is 50% of all documents rather than the paper's literal '50% normal documents' - a small, disclosed deviation documented in A12 whose test-set size, anomaly count and 10% anomaly rate match the paper. The measured token AUROC is 0.6137 versus the paper's 0.6371, i.e. 0.0234 low and just outside the +/-0.02 tolerance; across seeds 42/0/1/2 the value spans 0.5633-0.6295 (std 0.0248), so the paper number lies within ~1 sd of the reproduced distribution and the residual gap is best explained by split randomness plus under-specified details, most notably A14 (the paper text names bert-base-uncased while the released notebook uses bert-base-cased), which could account for the small systematic component since even the best seed stays ~0.008 below the paper value. Anti-cheat is clean: paper_numbers_found_in_code is empty, the 0.6371 target is read only from state/plan.json for the pass/fail band and never reported as a result, all metrics are computed at runtime from the released data, and a random-score control yields AUROC 0.4945. Nothing was scaled down (full 300-document benchmark, 1,419 test tokens, four seeds) and no core component of the proposed method was substituted. The uncovered items are the six baseline detectors (R8) and the SMS_Spam/Review datasets, neither of which is part of the C1 match target.

requirement_check.evidence: Primary run uses bert-base-uncased (last hidden state) with element-wise max pooling, i.e. exactly the shared representation R1 prescribes, and the pooling is unit-checked ('sandcastle', 2 subwords, doc 46 = coordinate-wise max; batch-invariance max|solo-batched| ~3e-6). However, only TokenCore was run: none of the six comparison methods were executed, so the 'all methods ... so that only the detection algorithm differs' clause is untested.

pooling_unit_check asserts the stored word vector equals np.max over its subword last_hidden_state vectors and explicitly asserts it is NOT the first subword and NOT the mean of subwords (A4/A14 axes settled from the authors' notebook: last layer, no normalization, all word units kept).
Memory bank = all 1,327 word-level token embeddings of the 150 normal training documents; the code asserts int(z_train.sum())==0, i.e. no anomalous token embedding enters the bank.

Token score = Euclidean L2 distance to the single nearest neighbour in the bank (sklearn NearestNeighbors, n_neighbors=1); sanity shows mean test NN distance 10.04 > mean train self-excluded NN distance 9.28, and the random-score control gives AUROC 0.4945.
Document score = mean of token scores (Eq. 3); doc AUROC mean-agg = 0.5678. The authors' eval.py np.max variant is reported as a diagnostic (0.4733) but is not used for the primary value.

The run uses the authors' recovered split_anomaly_data (random_state=42): n_train = int(0.5*300) = 150 documents drawn from the 270 normal ones (i.e. 55.6% of normal docs, not the 50% of normal documents the paper text states, which would be 135); test = remaining 120 normal + all 30 anomalous. Test-set size, anomaly count and class balance match the paper (300 docs, 30 anomalous, 10%), and the deviation is disclosed in assumption A12 as the authors' own code.

metrics.json reports token AUROC 0.6137, token AUPRC 0.0380 (average-precision check 0.0390), document AUROC mean-agg 0.5678 and document AUPRC mean-agg 0.2095 — both metrics at both levels for the reproduced dataset.

LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder and LUNAR were never run; only TokenCore is evaluated, so no comparison table was produced. (Out of scope for the C1 match target, which is a TokenCore cell.)

A tokenizer-level census over all 300 documents asserts a 1:1 gold-token -> word-unit mapping (word_ids == range(len(doc)) per document) before any scoring, so scores align with the word-level annotations.
Data loaded from the released repo/data/grammar.npy; asserts n_docs==300 and n_test_anom_docs==30, i.e. 30 anomalous / 300 documents = 10% anomaly rate, 2,746 tokens with 47 positive tokens (1.71%).
Document labels are derived as any(token label)=1 per document and passed as the y vector to split_anomaly_data and to the document-level metric, keeping document and token labels consistent.
